# agentplan

> A shared to-do list for AI agents. Zero dependencies, pure Python. v0.5.0.

agentplan is a CLI task queue that gives AI agents a persistent, dependency-aware ticket system with role-based routing, event hooks, and a dashboard control plane. Any agent that can run shell commands can use it — no SDK, no framework, no runtime required.

## When to use agentplan

Use agentplan when you need to:
- Coordinate multiple AI agents working on the same project
- Route tickets to the right agent based on roles (coding, research, writing, etc.)
- Break complex work into tickets with dependencies that auto-unblock
- Set up event hooks that fire when tickets complete (webhooks, commands, agent chains)
- Handle crashed agents with claim timeouts and automatic reaping
- Track which agent did what (attribution on every ticket)
- Run autonomous build loops where agents claim and complete work
- Give an agent a structured backlog instead of free-form instructions

## Install

```bash
pip install agentplan
```

## Quick start (copy-paste this)

```bash
# Auto-detect installed AI tools
agentplan init

# Create a project with tickets
agentplan create "Build my app" \
  --ticket "Set up database schema" \
  --ticket "Build API endpoints" \
  --ticket "Write tests"

# Add dependencies — tests need API
agentplan depend build-my-app 3 --on 2

# Tag tickets with roles for routing
agentplan ticket edit build-my-app 1 --tag role:coding
agentplan ticket edit build-my-app 2 --tag role:coding

# Route a ticket to the right agent
agentplan route build-my-app 1
# → codex (matched role:coding)

# Claim with a timeout (agent has 30 min)
agentplan claim build-my-app --agent codex --timeout 30

# Mark it done
agentplan ticket done build-my-app 1 --agent codex

# Check status
agentplan status build-my-app
```

## The agent loop pattern

```
1. ticket = agentplan next <project>        # What should I work on?
2. [do the work]                             # Agent executes the task
3. agentplan ticket done <project> <id>      # Mark complete (hooks fire)
4. agentplan ticket add <project> "..."      # Add follow-up work if needed
5. repeat until queue is empty
```

## Key commands

| Command | What it does |
|---------|-------------|
| `agentplan init` | Auto-detect installed AI tools and register agents |
| `agentplan create <title>` | Create a project |
| `agentplan ticket add <project> <title>` | Add a ticket (supports --priority, --tag, --desc, --due) |
| `agentplan next <project>` | Get next unblocked ticket (auto-reaps stale claims first) |
| `agentplan ticket done <project> <id>` | Mark ticket done (supports --agent, --note) |
| `agentplan ticket block <project> <id>` | Mark ticket blocked (--reason) |
| `agentplan ticket fail <project> <id>` | Mark ticket failed (--reason) |
| `agentplan depend <project> <id> --on <id>` | Add dependency |
| `agentplan status <project>` | Show project progress |
| `agentplan claim <project>` | Atomically claim next ticket (--timeout for expiry) |
| `agentplan reap <project>` | Reclaim expired/stale claims |
| `agentplan role add <name>` | Create a role (coding, research, etc.) |
| `agentplan agent add <name>` | Register an agent with command template and roles |
| `agentplan route <project> <id>` | Route a ticket to the matching agent |
| `agentplan hook add <project>` | Add on-complete hook (command, webhook, or chain) |
| `agentplan search "<query>"` | Search tickets across all projects |
| `agentplan dashboard` | Launch web UI with control plane |

## Roles & Routing

```bash
# Define roles
agentplan role add coding --description "Code implementation"
agentplan role add research --description "Research tasks"

# Register agents with command templates and roles
agentplan agent add codex --command 'codex exec {ticket}' --roles coding --priority 1
agentplan agent add claude --command 'claude -m {ticket}' --roles research,writing --priority 2

# Tag tickets → agentplan routes to the right agent
agentplan ticket edit myproject 1 --tag role:coding
agentplan route myproject 1
# → codex
```

## Event Hooks

```bash
# Fire a command when any ticket completes
agentplan hook add myproject --event on-complete --type command --target 'echo {ticket} done!'

# Fire a webhook
agentplan hook add myproject --event on-complete --type webhook --target 'https://hooks.slack.com/...'

# Chain to next agent
agentplan hook add myproject --event on-complete --type chain --target 'agentplan claim myproject --agent next'
```

## Stale Claim Handling

```bash
# Claim with timeout
agentplan claim myproject --agent builder --timeout 30

# Manually reap expired claims
agentplan reap myproject

# Auto-reap happens on every `next` call
agentplan next myproject
```

## Ticket States

```
pending → in-progress → done | blocked | failed | needs-review
blocked → pending | in-progress
failed → pending | in-progress
```

## Output formats

- `--format compact` — single line, token-efficient for prompt injection
- `--format json` — machine-readable for programmatic use
- Default — human-readable board view

## Features

- Dependency graph with auto-unblock and cycle detection
- Role-based routing with agent priorities
- Agent registry with command templates
- Event hooks (commands, webhooks, chains)
- Stale claim handling with timeouts and auto-reap
- Validated state machine (blocked, failed, needs-review)
- Auto-detection of installed AI tools
- Dashboard control plane (Start/Stop, Kanban, Agents page, review panel)
- Priority levels (high/medium/low) with smart ordering
- Tags for filtering and role routing
- Subtasks, due dates, audit logs, agent attribution
- Parallel-safe claims (SQLite BEGIN IMMEDIATE)
- Shell completions (bash/zsh/fish)
- Zero runtime dependencies (Flask optional for dashboard)
- 186 tests

## Configuration

- `AGENTPLAN_DB` — override database path (default: ~/.agentplan/agentplan.db)
- `AGENTPLAN_DIR` — override data directory (default: ~/.agentplan)
